reason: C0 is a load/compensation capacitor that mainly shapes bandwidth/phase margin; removing it usually preserves DC amplification behavior. Caveat: stability and transient ringing can worsen, and UGF/noise may change if this was intentional compensation.

R1 appears to provide a bleed/DC reference for the internal node net015; if net015 already has a defined DC path through M3 and R0, R1 can often be removed without breaking basic operation. Caveat: net015 may float at startup/leakage, increasing offset or slowing settling.

M10 is a diode-connected PMOS tied to net013 and likely serves as a bias/helper device for the PMOS load; in many cases the main load action is provided by M11 to VOUT1, so removing M10 can still leave a functioning single-ended stage. Caveat: operating point and gain can shift because M10 may be setting net013’s DC level/bias current; removing it may reduce bias stability.
